note: Canada's provinces and territories. The federal frame is Criminal Code s.207, which lets each province conduct and manage gambling in its own territory — so there is no national online casino law and the answer genuinely differs by province. `model` and its sources are what we can cite today. `provincialOperator` and `regulator` are recorded only where sourced; a province with nulls means we have not yet read its own body's page, not that it has none. Operator-level availability is NOT here: it comes from each casino's own terms via data/restricted.json, so a province's page shows who says they will not serve it. Sourced provinces were read from the named body's own site on 2026-10-01; the rest still show only the model that follows from the Criminal Code.

federal.summary: The Criminal Code prohibits gambling except where a provincial government conducts and manages it. Every province therefore runs, or licenses, its own online gambling — and what is legal for you depends on the province you are in, not on Canada.

provinces.name: Ontario
provinces.summary: The only province that has run an open licensed market for years. Private operators register with the AGCO and sign an operating agreement with iGaming Ontario before they may offer games to Ontarians.

regulator.name: Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO), with iGaming Ontario

provinces.name: Alberta
provinces.summary: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis runs Play Alberta and, since the market opened in 2026, maintains a public register of iGaming operators and suppliers alongside it.

provinces.name: British Columbia
provinces.summary: British Columbia Lottery Corporation runs the only legal online casino in the province. PlayNow states on its own site that it is the official gaming site for BC residents, operated by BCLC.

provinces.name: Québec
provinces.summary: Loto-Québec runs the province's only legal online casino through its own portal, which carries its online games directly.

provinces.name: Manitoba
provinces.summary: Manitoba Liquor & Lotteries runs the province's gambling, and lists PlayNow among its own operations alongside the Casinos of Winnipeg.
